paras: The lynching of James Fox took place in August 1915 at the camp of the Alger-Sullivan Lumber Company, eight miles north of Tunnel Springs, Alabama, where a mob pursued, shot and hanged a Black man accused of wounding a deputy sheriff. The only account came from a special dispatch to the Mobile Item, which was reprinted in Alabama, Tennessee and South Carolina and condensed into one-line items in Wisconsin and Kentucky weeklies.

According to the Tunnel Springs dispatch, a deputy sheriff was stationed at the lumber company's camp, and his name "could not be learned" by the correspondent. The man accused was identified only as "a negro named Fox" in the dispatch, while later briefs gave his full name as James Fox.

Fox was accused of having "shot and dangerously wounded" the deputy at the camp. Shortly afterward a mob gathered and "entered upon a successful pursuit" of him. Once caught, he was shot and then hanged, although "reports here state that he was dead before he was strung up." The dispatch, dated Tunnel Springs, August 9, placed the lynching on the previous night, August 8.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage, and the condition of the wounded deputy was not reported again.

The Montgomery Advertiser printed the Mobile story on its front page on August 10 under the headline "Negro Lynched for Attacking Officer," presenting the accusation as fact and offering no comment on the mob. Three days later the Columbia Herald in Tennessee ran the same text, re-dated August 10, as "Shoots Officer Negro Lynched," with a deck reading "Mob Gathers, First Shoots and Then Strings Him Up." The Watchman and Southron of Sumter, South Carolina, cut it to two sentences under "Negro Put to Death."

Farther away the story shrank to a single line in syndicated news roundups. Wisconsin weeklies, including the Wauwatosa News, the Eagle River Review and the Wausau Pilot, reported only that James Fox had been lynched at the lumber company camp, with no mention of the shooting. Kentucky papers, the Climax-Madisonian and the Hazard Herald, listed him among "Bunched Paragraphs" as "colored" and lynched after wounding "a deputy marshal." No Black-press account of the lynching appears in the coverage, which rests entirely on the Mobile dispatch and its condensations.
The Alabama dispatch called the wounded officer a deputy sheriff, while the Kentucky brief called him a deputy marshal; the fuller dispatch is the closer source.

reader.title: Lynching of James Fox
bases: A mob pursued, shot and hanged a Black man accused of wounding a deputy sheriff (A1, A2).

Fox was shot and hanged by a 'mob' that gathered and pursued him after he was accused of shooting a deputy (A1, A2); no lawful authority is mentioned, and every report calls it a lynching (A1, A6, A8).
All reports, including the briefs (A3, A8), trace to one Mobile Item special from Tunnel Springs (A1); no independent local, official or Black-press account was found.

accounts.label: Mobile Item special from Tunnel Springs
accounts.gist: Fox shot and dangerously wounded a deputy at the lumber camp; a mob gathered, pursued him, shot him and then hanged him, though local reports said he was already dead when hanged.

accounts.label: National news-roundup briefs
accounts.gist: One-sentence items naming him James Fox; one omits the accusation, another says he had wounded a 'deputy marshal'.

framing.detail: The Montgomery Advertiser ran the Item special on page one as 'Negro Lynched for Attacking Officer', giving the accusation as fact and no comment on the mob.
The Columbia Herald headlined 'Shoots officer negro lynched / Mob gathers, first shoots and then strings him up'; the Sumter paper used 'Negro Put to Death'.
Northern weeklies reduced it to a single line in syndicated news roundups.

conflicts.note: The fuller Alabama-origin dispatch says deputy sheriff; the one-line Kentucky brief is a condensed rewrite.
The Advertiser printed the story on Aug. 10 under an Aug. 9 dateline, so the Aug. 10 datelines in later reprints are probably re-dated copies.

record_check.dossier: Night of 1915-08-08: the Aug. 9 dispatch printed Aug. 10 says 'last night'; Aug. 10 is a reprint dateline.
Alger-Sullivan Lumber Co. camp, eight miles north of Tunnel Springs (Tunnel Springs is the dateline).
Not in custody: the mob pursued and caught him after the shooting.
Shot, then hanged (reportedly already dead when hanged).
One deputy sheriff reported dangerously wounded (race not stated).

info: The night before an Aug. 9 dispatch ('last night'), i.e. the night of Aug. 8, 1915; one reprint dates the dispatch Aug. 10
Camp of the Alger-Sullivan Lumber Co., eight miles north of Tunnel Springs
A Black man named Fox; 'James Fox' in two briefs
Accused of shooting and dangerously wounding a deputy sheriff stationed at the lumber camp ('deputy marshal' in one brief)
A mob that gathered shortly after the shooting; members not named
